subject.title: [Bug]: Hybrid memory search returns spurious 1.0 similarity scores via FTS LIKE-fallback hard-coded textScore

question: Should a LIKE fallback be represented as a bounded lower-confidence lexical signal, or is a normalized score of 1 an intentional binary-match contract that must instead be isolated from hybrid ranking?
rationale: The evidence identifies a plausible defect but does not establish the intended semantics of fallback relevance; choosing a replacement score or merge policy affects existing retrieval ranking.

options.title: Define a lower-confidence fallback score
options.body: Treat LIKE fallback as a weaker lexical signal, add a deterministic regression test, and preserve BM25 behavior for normal MATCH queries.

options.title: Keep binary LIKE scoring but isolate it
options.body: Retain a score of 1 for exact fallback matching but prevent it from combining with vector scoring as a perfect hybrid result.

options.title: Document the current contract
options.body: Keep the current behavior only if maintainers confirm that a LIKE hit intentionally represents perfect lexical relevance in hybrid ranking.

recommendation.title: Define a lower-confidence fallback score
recommendation.body: Treat LIKE fallback as a weaker lexical signal, add a deterministic regression test, and preserve BM25 behavior for normal MATCH queries.
